- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to account for reversal.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or apply decay factor.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 50% of 30d moving avg), model tends to lag; add 1–3 days of downward bias.  
- For 30d forecasts, if history shows high volatility (std > 3% of mean), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; match forecast slope to sentiment trend.
